CLI reference

Usage emitted by the built tunn binary.

Regenerate with make docs-cli; verify with make test-docs. Global flags precede the subcommand. Serve flags can follow the target. Sharing commands have no separate help page; their usage below comes from invoking them without arguments. TCP, Unix and connect currently print a short usage on help. Service flags shown are for service install; run the chosen action with --help. Host-manifest defaults use Linux paths in this generated reference; check local help on macOS or Windows.

tunn --help

tunn - expose localhost to the internet

Usage:
  tunn <port>                    Tunnel localhost:<port> to a public URL
  tunn <host:port>               Tunnel host:port to a public URL
  tunn <url>                     Tunnel any URL to a public URL
  tunn service install|uninstall|restart|status|check  Manage persistent machine endpoints
  tunn hosts [--json]             List your machines and their tunnels
  tunn openclaw [options]         Preview OpenClaw phone setup (needs WebSockets)
  tunn keys add|list|remove       Manage account SSH public keys
  tunn login                     Authenticate with GitHub
  tunn serve [options] <target>  Explicit serve mode (same as default)
  tunn http [options] <target>   Shortcut for ngrok-style HTTP usage
  tunn mcp [options] <command…>   Connect a local MCP server to an AI agent
  tunn connector-check [options] <url>  Diagnose a private MCP connector
  tunn tcp [options] <host:port>  Publish a private raw TCP endpoint
  tunn unix [options] <path>      Publish a private Unix socket
  tunn connect [options] <name>   Open a remote TCP endpoint locally
  tunn token [--rotate] <name>   Print or rotate an endpoint access token
  tunn ip-policy <action>        Manage endpoint or account IP restrictions
  tunn usage <name>              Export caller usage and audit decisions
  tunn share <name> <recipient>  Share web access: email or group:ORG:GROUP
  tunn unshare <name> <recipient> Revoke web access and active streams
  tunn access <name>             Show who has access
  tunn grant create <name>       Issue a metered, expiring consumer token
  tunn grant revoke <name> <id>  Revoke one consumer grant
  tunn domain add|verify|list|delete  Manage Pro custom domains
  tunn status serve|incident|resolve  Relay probe history and local incident notes
  tunn admin --help             Local authenticated account and billing controls

Examples:
  tunn 8080                              # https://abc123.tunn.to -> localhost:8080
  tunn 8080 --allow=alice@gmail.com      # Share with specific people
  tunn localhost:3000                    # Tunnel localhost:3000
  tunn http://api.local:9000             # Tunnel any URL
  tunn mcp -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem .
  tunn tcp --name database localhost:5432
  tunn unix --name docker /var/run/docker.sock
  tunn connect --listen 127.0.0.1:15432 database

Options:
  -cert string
        TLS certificate file (host mode) (default "/app/certs/fullchain.pem")
  -dev
        use development configuration (or set TUNN_ENV=dev)
  -domain string
        public apex domain (default "tunn.to")
  -insecure
        skip TLS verification for proxy gRPC connection (insecure)
  -key string
        TLS private key file (host mode) (default "/app/certs/privkey.pem")
  -mode string
        internal: host mode for server operators
  -verbosity string
        log level: none, error, request, trace (default "request")

tunn http --help

Usage: tunn serve [options] <port|host:port|url>
       tunn <target> [options]

Options:
  --id, --name, --subdomain NAME  Tunnel name (blank generates one)
  --allow EMAILS                 Comma-separated email allow-list
  --bearer                       Enable endpoint tokens for HTTP and WebSockets
  --require-upstream-auth        Require application Authorization after tunn auth
  --verify-webhook PROVIDER      Stripe, GitHub, Slack, Shopify or hmac-sha256 (lowercase)
  --webhook-secret-file PATH     Private signing-secret file (mode 0600)
  --webhook-tolerance DURATION   Signed timestamp tolerance (default 5m; 1s to 1h)
  --ws-idle-timeout DURATION     WebSocket inactivity timeout (default 5m; 0 disables)
  --ws-keepalive DURATION        Ping interval (default 30s; 0 disables)
  --ws-max-message-size BYTES    Message limit across fragments (default 8388608)
  --inspect                     Open a local metadata inspector
  --inspect-body                Retain local bodies up to 64 KiB (requires --inspect)
  --skip-local-tls-verify        Skip local HTTPS certificate verification
  --secret SECRET               Self-hosted publisher secret (or TUNN_SECRET)
  --tunnel-key KEY               Tunnel creation authorization key

tunn mcp --help

tunn mcp - expose a local stdio MCP server

Usage:
  tunn mcp [options] <command> [args...]
  tunn mcp [options] -- <command> [args...]
  tunn mcp [options] <http-url>

Examples:
  tunn mcp --tools echo -- python3 examples/mcp/echo.py
  tunn mcp --name work -- docker mcp gateway run --profile work
  tunn mcp --name local http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp
  tunn mcp --public -- ./my-mcp-server

Options:
  --name, --id <name>       Endpoint name (blank generates one)
  --allow <emails>          Share with additional tunn account emails
  --public                  Explicitly allow unauthenticated access
  --tools <names>           Exact comma-separated tool allow-list (stdio only)
  --tunnel-key <key>        Tunnel creation authorization key
  --secret <secret>         Self-hosted client authentication secret

After publishing, run tunn connector-check --oauth --expect-tools echo <Connector-URL>.
Guide: https://tunn.to/mcp-to-claude

tunn connector-check --help

tunn connector-check - diagnose a private MCP connector

Usage:
  tunn connector-check [options] <https-connector-url/mcp>

Default: check the HTTPS challenge and OAuth/PKCE metadata without registering a client.
  --oauth                 Register a diagnostic client; print a browser consent link
  --expect-tools <names>  Assert the exact comma-separated exposed tool set (requires --oauth)
  --call-tool <name>      Invoke one explicitly chosen harmless tool (requires --oauth)
  --arguments <json>      JSON object for --call-tool (default {})
  --deny-tool <name>      Probe a harmless blocked tool; require tunn's -32001 denial
  --timeout <duration>    Total deadline including browser consent (default 3m, max 10m)
  --json                  Print a structured final report; consent link goes to stderr

Examples:
  tunn connector-check https://my-tools.tunn.to/mcp
  tunn connector-check --oauth --expect-tools echo --call-tool echo --arguments '{"message":"hello"}' https://my-tools.tunn.to/mcp

Both call probes must be harmless even if policy is broken. No tool is called by default.
OAuth tokens stay in memory. Disconnect “tunn connector-check” at /account/mcp afterward.
Guide: https://tunn.to/mcp-to-claude

tunn usage --help

Usage:
  tunn usage [--tunnel NAME] [--since DURATION]
  tunn grant create <endpoint> [--for email] [--expires 1h]
       [--rate requests-per-minute] [--monthly-requests N] [--monthly-bytes N]
  tunn grant revoke <endpoint> <grant-id>
  tunn grant list [<endpoint>]
Owner API options: --server, --owner-token-file, --insecure
Usage defaults to the current UTC month across all of the owner's tunnels.
The positional usage endpoint and --month YYYY-MM remain supported.
Zero budgets mean unlimited. Create prints JSON containing the grant and its
one-time consumer token; only the token's SHA-256 digest reaches the relay.

tunn domain --help

Usage:
  tunn domain add <domain> --tunnel <reserved-name>
  tunn domain add '*.apps.example.com' [--tunnel <app-name>]
  tunn domain verify <domain>
  tunn domain list
  tunn domain delete <domain>
Owner options: --server, --owner-token-file, --insecure
Add requires Pro and returns a unique cname_target. Set your DNS CNAME to
that exact target, then run verify to provision HTTPS. Wildcard claims can
instead prove ownership with TXT _tunn-verification.<suffix> = cname_target;
route the DNS-only wildcard CNAME to the edge. Verify checks ownership, and
HTTPS is issued on demand for each owner-reserved app name. Repeating wildcard
add with --tunnel reserves another app name under the existing claim. Publish the reserved
name with tunn serve --name <reserved-name> <target>. List shows DNS and
certificate state. Delete removes the domain; the tunnel name stays reserved.

tunn keys add <public-key-file> | list | remove <SHA256:fingerprint>

tunn ip-policy --help

tunn ip-policy <get|set|clear> [endpoint | --account] [options]
  --allow CIDR,...        IPv4/IPv6 allow list (set only)
  --deny CIDR,...         IPv4/IPv6 deny list (set only; deny takes priority)
  --server HTTPS_ORIGIN  Relay origin
  --owner-token-file PATH  Owner JWT file (publisher device tokens cannot manage policies)
Set replaces both lists. Empty lists permit every IP. Clear restores inheritance
for an endpoint or removes the account default. Policies apply to new requests.

tunn admin --help

tunn admin <action> --db PATH --admin-config PATH --token-file PATH
Actions: status, suspend, resume, billing-bind, billing-status, billing-events, reconcile,
         report-intake, report-respond, fixture-init, migrate, reconcile-legacy, payment-queue, payment-review
Account operations: --account UUID --expect-version N --reason TEXT
Billing bind: --account UUID --provider NAME --customer ID --subscription ID
Billing status: --subscription ID [--after provider/subscription] (payments_next continues account payments)
Billing fixtures: --events PATH (disposable fixture databases only)
Reconcile: --snapshots PATH [--apply-fixture | --apply-reviewed] (default: read-only dry run)
Reviewed apply requires fresh Stripe evidence and receipts; see GO-LIVE.md.
Legacy reconciliation: --snapshots PATH (explicit decisions; requires accounts:["*"])
Payment queue: [--after provider/subscription] (100 records per page)
Payment review: --snapshots PATH (one reasoned CAS decision; see docs/revenue/round3-fixes.md)
Reports: --account UUID --category abuse|billing|availability --endpoint NAME
Response: --report ID --response triaged|action_taken|closed --expect-version N
Fixture init: --email fixture@example.invalid (creates a new disposable database)
Credentials: owner-only JSON [{"actor":"operator","token_sha256":"HEX","accounts":["UUID"]}]
No network, provider writes, mail, or public administration endpoint.
